article.headline: From eMule to MoMA PS1: DJ Marfox and Lisbon's batida
article.standfirst: Born Marlon Silva in Lisbon in June 1988 to parents from São Tomé e Príncipe, DJ Marfox is credited with pioneering batida, the "ghetto sound of Lisbon" that came out of the city's housing estates. It fuses kuduro, kizomba, funaná and tarraxinha with house and techno.
body: DJ Marfox, born Marlon Silva in Lisbon in June 1988 to parents from São Tomé e Príncipe, is best known for pioneering batida, the "ghetto sound of Lisbon" that came out of the city's housing estates. It fuses African-influenced dance music such as kuduro, kizomba, funaná and tarraxinha with house and techno.

He has DJed as Marfox since 2002. The name joins "Marl" from Marlon with Star Fox, a Nintendo character he played as a teenager. In 2005 he founded DJs do Guetto with DJ Pausas and DJ Fofuxo. A year later the crew put DJs do Ghetto Vol. I, a 37-track digital compilation, on eMule. Príncipe Discos has since reissued it as a free download, and it is seen as the founding release of the ghetto sound of Lisbon.

His first solo album, Eu sei quem Eu Sou (I Know Who I Am), came out on Príncipe Discos in early 2011. Philip Sherburne described it as "an atomic field of taut drums, hiccupping yelps, zapping synths and pinprick details." Artist Unknown (Pollinaire, 2012) and Subliminar (Enchufada, 2013) followed.

In 2014 his Lucky Punch EP on Lit City Trax made Dazed's top ten albums for August. He played Red Bull Music Academy in New York, and on 30 August he played MoMA PS1's Warm Up series. Rolling Stone also named him among its "10 New Artists You Need to Know" that year. Cedar Pasori wrote that the PS1 appearance "reinforced the accelerating spread of Afro-Portuguese dance music around the world."

On 13 March 2015 Warp announced the Cargaa 1 EP for 7 April, with Marfox as its central figure. Three days later Revolução 2005–2008, a collection of tracks he made in his bedroom in those years, came out on CD and as a free download. One of his first international collaborations was a rework of tUnE-yArDs' "Water Fountain" featuring the Brazilian band Pearls Negras. His Chapa Quente EP includes "Tarraxo Everyday".

points.text: In 2014 came Red Bull Music Academy in New York, Rolling Stone's "10 New Artists You Need to Know" and MoMA PS1's Warm Up on 30 August. In spring 2015 Warp's Cargaa 1 EP put him at its centre.

article.headline: DJ Nigga Fox and Príncipe's disorienting polyrhythms
article.standfirst: Rogério Brandão Luís was born in Luanda in 1990 and moved to Lisbon at four. He made his first beats on a computer in his bedroom on the city's outskirts.
body: DJ Nigga Fox has taken the disorienting polyrhythms of Lisbon's Afro-Portuguese diaspora from Lux Frágil, Musicbox, Iminente and Porto's Hard Club to Berghain, Sónar, Club to Club, H0L0 in New York and WWW in Tokyo. Príncipe discovered him and started releasing his music in 2011. Since then Rogério Brandão Luís has become one of the leading artists to emerge from Portugal's Afro-descendant communities.

He was born in Luanda in 1990 to a Congolese mother and an Angolan father, and moved to Lisbon with his parents and older brother at four. He grew up on the outskirts of the city and started building beats and melodies on a computer in his bedroom.
His music starts from kuduro, afro house, tarraxinha and batida and pushes them into experimental polyrhythms. Pitchfork, The Wire and Trax Magazine have all recognised his work more than once.

Wider attention came in stages. In early 2015, when few people knew Príncipe or its releases, Thom Yorke of Radiohead shared a list of tracks he was listening to. It included "Weed" alongside producers like Kool A.D. and Bernard Parmegiani. In 2016, British filmmakers Tim & Barry premiered "Sons do Gueto", a documentary about Príncipe and the African-influenced electronic music made in Lisbon's suburbs and social housing estates. It presented him as one of the label's faces.

He has also worked in film. He contributed to the soundtracks of Pedro Costa's "Vitalina Varela" and Rita Maia and Vasco Viana's "Batida de Lisboa", and his music was part of the opening of Copenhagen's CPH:DOX festival in 2020.

His Warp Records debut came in 2014 with "LUMI" on the CARGAA 1 compilation, followed by Crânio in 2018. On Príncipe, his catalogue runs from O Meu Estilo EP (2013) through Noite E Dia (2015) and 15 Barras (2017) to Cartas Na Manga (2019).

article.headline: Branko: the Lisbon producer wiring up global club music
article.standfirst: Branko, the alias of Portuguese DJ and producer João Barbosa, built his 2015 debut album Atlas from travels around Cape Town, New York, Amsterdam and São Paulo. Princess Nokia, DJ Sliink and Rodes Rollins all appear on it.
body: Branko is the solo name of João Barbosa, a Portuguese DJ and producer born on 28 November 1980. His records connect club music from several continents, and his label and radio show are run out of Lisbon. He first became known as part of Buraka Som Sistema and previously went by J-Wow.

His debut album as Branko, Atlas, came out in 2015. It was inspired by his travels around Cape Town, New York, Amsterdam and São Paulo, and featured Princess Nokia and DJ Sliink, plus Rodes Rollins on "Out Of Sight (So Right)".

The network kept growing. "Let Me Go", with Mr. Carmack and Nonku Phiri, was picked up by i-D, Hypebeast and The Fader. Rolling Stone announced his second solo album, Nosso, on 22 January 2019. Its guests include Sango, Cosima, Mallu Magalhães, Dino d'Santiago, Catalina García of Monsieur Periné, Pierre Kwenders, Miles From Kinshasa, Umi Copper, PEDRO and Dengue Dengue Dengue. Outside his own releases, he worked with M.I.A. on her 2016 album AIM and has also worked with Santigold and Anik Khan.

Lisbon is the base for all of it. Branko hosts Enchufada Na Zona, a monthly show on NTS broadcast live from the Lisbon headquarters of the label Enchufada. The show inspired a compilation of the same name. In 2018 he was also one of the interval acts at the Eurovision Song Contest final in Lisbon.
His most recent chapter came in 2024, when he released the single "Slide" featuring Jay Prince, building up to the release of his album SOMA in March that year.

article.headline: Pete Tha Zouk: Locomia to DJ Mag's No. 37
article.standfirst: On 20 October 2011, Pete Tha Zouk climbed 44 places in the DJ Mag Top 100, from 81 to 37. No Portuguese DJ had ever placed higher.
body: On 20 October 2011, Pete Tha Zouk was announced at number 37 in the DJ Mag Top 100. He had entered the chart at 81 the year before, so he climbed 44 places. It was the highest position a Portuguese DJ had ever reached.

His education came from the booth. António Pedro was born in Olhão in 1978 and started as a resident at two venues: Mitto, a bar that changed how the South starts its nights, and Locomia, the seafront club on Santa Eulália beach. All the world's best-known DJs played Locomia during the summer seasons, and Pete got to watch them work up close.

His first tracks, 'First Tribal Feeling' with Bruno Marciano and 'Kashmira', were big dancefloor hits in the early 2000s. 'First Tribal Feeling' caught the attention of Chus, and soon afterwards Pete was in Madrid mastering it at the Chus & Ceballos studio. 'Kashmira' and 'Enchantments' followed and made his name as a producer for the floor.

In 2003 he and DJ Vibe released 'Solid Textures' on Low Pressings. The track topped the charts, and at the 2004 Dance Club awards it won Single of the Year while Pete was named Best Producer. The same magazine had named him DJ Revelação in 2002.

In 2006 he joined the agency WDB, which took his career to Brazil, Switzerland and Angola. His first gig outside Portugal was New Year 2010/11 in Brazil. In 2010 he released 'Check This Out' on Sondos, Erick Morillo's label, and that same year made his DJ Mag Top 100 debut at 81.

points.title: The WDB years
points.text: He joined WDB in 2006 and became Portugal's most in-demand DJ. Promoters knew his name meant 'casa cheia', a full house. WDB then took him to Brazil, Switzerland and Angola.

points.title: The awards
points.text: In 2004 Dance Club named him Best Producer and gave 'Solid Textures' Single of the Year. He won Melhor DJ Português at the Prémios Noite.pt in 2005, 2006, 2008, 2009 and 2010.

points.text: 'First Tribal Feeling' (with Bruno Marciano), 'Kashmira', 'Solid Textures' (2003, with DJ Vibe, Low Pressings), 'Check This Out' (2010, Erick Morillo's Sondos), 'I'm Back Again' (2010, with Mastercris and Abigail Bailey).

article.headline: SoundCloud cracks down on AI slop and spam
article.standfirst: SoundCloud is cracking down on what it calls "AI slop, spam, and excessive uploads", according to Music Business Worldwide.
body: SoundCloud is cracking down on what it calls "AI slop, spam, and excessive uploads", Music Business Worldwide reports. The platform has introduced new terms aimed at users who use AI to game its systems.

Under the updated terms, SoundCloud can withhold, reverse or recover payouts from those users. That covers the whole payment cycle: money can be held back before it is paid, cancelled, or recovered after it has already been paid out.

The timing stands out. The crackdown comes only weeks after SoundCloud struck AI deals with Moises and ElevenLabs. So the platform is partnering with AI companies on one side and setting financial penalties for AI misuse on the other.

SoundCloud has long been a home base for DJs and producers sharing tracks, edits and mixes. For anyone earning money from uploads there, the new terms tie payouts directly to how the platform's systems are used. Using AI to game those systems can now put that income at risk.

The three targets named in the crackdown are AI slop, spam and excessive uploads. Those are problems streaming services across the industry are trying to deal with as AI-generated audio becomes cheaper and faster to make.

article.headline: Kettama: from a Galway Launchpad to Radio 1
article.standfirst: Kettama is Evan Campbell, an Irish producer and DJ born in Galway in 1997. At 16 he bought a Launchpad, got an Ableton trial with it and taught himself by remaking the piano from Tyga's "I'm Different". Six months later he was on cracked FL Studio, uploading to SoundCloud.
body: Kettama, the Galway producer and DJ born Evan Campbell in 1997, has held a BBC Radio 1 Dance residency since 2025. On 29 May 2026 his single "Comes and Goes" entered the Irish Singles Chart at No. 19 and climbed to the top of the Irish Homegrown Chart.

He started out teaching himself. At 16, Campbell bought a Launchpad that came with an Ableton trial and experimented by remaking the piano from Tyga's "I'm Different". Six months later he downloaded a cracked copy of FL Studio and began uploading tracks to SoundCloud. By 17 he was playing clubs.

His breakthrough came in 2018 with "B O D Y", from the Bucklyn Bridge EP. It reached an international audience after Mall Grab and fellow Irish DJ Annie Mac played it often. A year later he co-founded G-Town Records with Shampain and named the label after Galway, the hometown they share.
Alongside his solo work, he performs and releases under collaborative aliases: Samba Boys with Tommy Holohan, and KETBOI69, a portmanteau project with Partiboi69.

In 2023 he played a sold-out homecoming show during the Galway International Arts Festival. In 2024 he made his debuts at Glastonbury, Coachella and Boomtown. On 5 June 2025, "It Gets Better (Forever Mix)" charted at No. 37 on the Irish Singles Chart, a year before "Comes and Goes" entered higher.
If you're new to him, start with "B O D Y", the track that broke him, then play "It Gets Better (Forever Mix)" and "Comes and Goes" to hear where his music has gone since.

article.headline: TIDAL to ban AI-generated tracks "entirely" next month
article.standfirst: TIDAL says it will ban AI-generated tracks "entirely" next month, per Mixmag.
body: TIDAL says it will ban AI-generated tracks from its platform "entirely" next month, Mixmag reports. The word "entirely" is the streaming service's own, quoted in Mixmag's headline.

The ban follows an earlier step. TIDAL says that since July it has labelled and demonetised 100% of all AI tracks on the platform. In other words, AI-generated music was marked as such and earned nothing.
A ban is a different kind of policy. Labelling and demonetising tells listeners what they are hearing and stops payments. A ban says this music isn't allowed on the service at all.

What the ban covers in practice isn't spelled out in the material available. It doesn't say whether tracks already on TIDAL will be taken down or whether the rule only applies to new uploads, or how TIDAL defines and detects an AI-generated track.

For producers and labels distributing music to TIDAL, including the many independent artists in Portugal who release through digital distributors, it's worth watching the details when the policy takes effect next month.

body: Nicolas Lutz has launched Integrador Dimensional, a new record label that will release music only on vinyl. He co-founded it with Fabiola Andriolo, Head of Projects at Polifonic.
The first record is 'Dharma Effect' by Nicolas Etorena, a producer born in Uruguay and based in Barcelona. It comes out on 15 January 2027, and pre-orders opened on 24 November 2026.
Integrador Dimensional is not built around a signature sound. The label aims to bring distinct musical identities together through shared sensibilities rather than a uniform sound.

For Lutz and Andriolo, the concept centres on intuition, curiosity and the relationships that can form between musical expressions that are otherwise different. So the catalogue is meant to grow through connections between artists, not around a genre template.

Mayze x Faria, Jonh Mayze and Miguel Faria, formed in Braga in 2004 and work across melodic techno, melodic house and tech house. They have played in Spain, Luxembourg, Colombia, Angola, Brazil and Mexico, and won the Talent Award from Portuguese platform 100% DJ in 2021.

article.headline: DJ Marfox took his name from Star Fox
article.standfirst: DJ Marfox, born Marlon Silva in Lisbon in June 1988 to parents from São Tomé e Príncipe, is best known for pioneering batida, the "ghetto sound of Lisbon" that mixes kuduro, kizomba, funaná and tarraxinha with house and techno.
body: Before he was one of the names that took Lisbon's sound around the world, DJ Marfox was a teenager playing Nintendo. The name joins "Marl", from his first name Marlon, with Star Fox, the character he played growing up.

Marlon Silva was born in Lisbon in June 1988 to parents from São Tomé e Príncipe and started deejaying as DJ Marfox in 2002. He is best known for pioneering batida, or batucada, the "ghetto sound of Lisbon" that came out of the city's housing estates and mixes African-influenced dance music such as kuduro, kizomba, funaná and tarraxinha with house and techno.

The scene's founding document wasn't pressed on vinyl. In 2005 he founded DJs do Guetto with DJ Pausas and DJ Fofuxo, and a year later they released DJs do Ghetto Vol. I, a 37-track digital compilation, on eMule. Príncipe Discos later re-issued it as a free download, and it is seen as the foundational release of the ghetto sound of Lisbon.

Príncipe also released his first solo album, Eu sei quem Eu Sou (I Know Who I Am), in early 2011. Philip Sherburne described it as "an atomic field of taut drums, hiccupping yelps, zapping synths and pinprick details."

In 2014 came the Lucky Punch EP on Lit City Trax, a Red Bull Music Academy performance in New York and a Warm Up show at MoMA PS1 on 30 August 2014. Rolling Stone also put him on its list of "10 New Artists You Need to Know".

In 2015 the bedroom tracks he made between 2005 and 2008 came out as Revolução 2005–2008, and WARP released Cargaa 1, an EP with DJ Marfox as its central figure. From a gamer tag and an eMule upload to one of Britain's best-known electronic labels, it's a very Lisbon story.

article.headline: Hannah Laing: from dental nurse to the doof
article.standfirst: Weekdays at the dental clinic, weekends on tour: Hannah Laing did both for 10 years. After a well-received Creamfields set in 2022, the Dundee DJ quit nursing and went full-time. She called the move "terrifying and freeing".
body: For ten years, Hannah Laing worked as a dental nurse during the week and toured at weekends. After a well-received set at Creamfields in 2022 she quit, and she has described going full-time as "terrifying and freeing". The Dundee DJ and producer now runs her own label, Doof, and her own festival.

Laing was born in Dundee in 1994. Her parents got her into rave music, and she played her first gig at 18 in an Arbroath venue. Fun fact: in 2007 she competed on CBBC's Raven and came fifth in the first week. While still nursing, she also held a DJ residency in San Antonio.

BBC Radio 1 helped her break through. Pete Tong and Danny Howard picked up on her, she played Radio 1's Big Weekend in 2022, and she headlined its dance stage in 2023. She has also recorded a two-hour Essential Mix. Her 2019 remix of Sophie Ellis-Bextor's Murder on the Dancefloor was played in DJ sets around the world. In 2023, Good Love with RoRo spent 26 weeks in the UK Singles Chart, peaked at number 7 and went Platinum. She has played TRNSMT, Creamfields and the Tidy Weekender, and she supported Idris Elba in Ibiza.

She calls her sound "doof", after the doof doof beat. The Into the Doof EP came out in July 2024. It was made over three days with other DJs, and she said it reflects "all the different styles I love". In July 2025 she launched Doof in the Park at Camperdown Country Park in Dundee. Around 15,000 people came, and Armin van Buuren, Judge Jules and Lisa Lashes were on the lineup. The festival returns in 2026.

That same year she held a residency at Hï Ibiza and released the Into the Bounce EP. In November 2025 she released Have You Ever Loved (Ellie), a tribute to her best friend, who had died earlier that year. It was her third Radio 1 Hottest Record, after Good Love and FWTDJ.

points.text: High-energy hard house, trance and techno, which she calls "doof" after the doof doof beat. She has played the Tidy Weekender and appears on TDV25 - The Remixes, the Tidy Trax tribute to hard house pioneer Tony De Vit.

points.text: In 2025 she launched Doof in the Park in Dundee (around 15,000 people, back in 2026), held a Hï Ibiza residency and released the Into the Bounce EP. Before that came a two-hour Essential Mix and a 2023 Big Weekend dance-stage headline.

body: Viseu gets a techno night this Saturday, and the whole profit goes to charity. Electronic Beira Sounds, organised by Dark Waves, takes over the Pavilhão Multiusos de Viseu, and every euro of profit goes to the Associação Humanitária de Bombeiros Voluntários de Viseu, the city's volunteer fire brigade.
The lineup is techno all night: Cravo b2b Vil, Du/art, Frank Maurel, Valody and Tryängle b2b VASQ.

The organisers have planned more than a stage and a dancefloor. There will be a bar, a food court and a chill out zone. There will also be a besafe space that raises awareness of risky behaviour. Harm reduction like this is still not standard at Portuguese events, and seeing it at a regional party is a good sign.

There's also a Creative HUB where local artists will give demos and sell their work. Add flash tattoos, a make-up artist, a hairdresser, crafts, custom t-shirts and a graffiti artist painting at the entrance, and it feels closer to a small festival than a normal club night.

The Município de Viseu supports the event through its Eixo Cultura programme. That matters. Electronic music outside Lisbon and Porto often has to fight for venues and recognition, and here a city hall is backing a techno event in a municipal pavilion.
For ravers in the Centro region, it's a reason to stay close to home this weekend. Everyone else should take note: the interior is building its own nights, and they come with a conscience.

body: Lisbon's coffee rave scene has a new kind of guest list. On Sunday, 29 November, Sundaze Morning Social brings its morning party to Connection Studio on Rua da Bempostinha with a special edition called "Paws On The Dance Floor". It runs from 11:00 to 14:00, and dogs from the Lisbon animal protection association União Zoófila will be there looking for new homes.

If you want to help, you can bring dog or cat food, donate money at the event or give directly to União Zoófila.

Sundaze Morning Social isn't new to this. The project turned one in June with a rooftop party at IDB Rooftop by Mīrārī in Marvila that mixed music with running and Pilates. This time it swaps the terrace for a café setting and adds a good cause.

Tickets are on sale online from €10, and late entry costs €12. Coffee raves keep growing in Lisbon, and this one is a reminder that the daytime crowd has its own rituals. Not every great pista needs a 6am finish.

Tresor's New Year's Week lasts six days, from 28 December to 2 January. It opens with a Floorplan and FJAAK showcase and a Minus night with Richie Hawtin and Marc Houle (live), and later brings Daniel Avery, Developer and Regis. body: Zohran Mamdani has appointed Rachael Pazdan as New York City's first-ever Director of Music, Mixmag reports.

Pazdan's brief is to work with the city's venues and musicians to "strengthen New York's music ecosystem". That is the role as Mixmag describes it. The report doesn't give details on her powers, her budget or where the post sits in the city's structure.

The brief is general. It covers music as a whole, and nothing in the report singles out nightlife, clubs or dance music. Still, venues are named as part of her job, and in a city like New York that list of venues includes the clubs. That reading is ours, not Mixmag's.

Why should you care from Portugal? Both halves of the brief are things the scene here talks about all the time: the rooms where music happens and the people who play in them. When a city the size of New York creates a dedicated post built around those two things, other cities can point to it.

HARDMAG's take: we don't know yet what Pazdan will actually do with the job, and the title alone fixes nothing. But one official whose brief is venues and the people who play them is an idea worth bringing up in Lisbon and Porto. We'll be watching what comes out of New York first.
